=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (successive compound leaves are attached at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides as seen in images 1, 2, and 4)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the length of the stem rather than clustered at the tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the leaf structure consists of a rachis bearing multiple leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (the leaflets are arranged along a central rachis and terminate in a single terminal leaflet, as seen in images 2, 3, and 4)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (one fully visible leaf in image 3 shows 4 pairs of leaflets, totaling 8 leaflets)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs along the rachis, as seen in images 2 and 3)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaflet margins appear smooth without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are oval-shaped, widest in the middle and tapering towards both ends, as seen in images 2 and 3)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the leaflet tips come to a distinct, relatively sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears rounded or slightly obtuse)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off from it, as seen in image 3)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, pinnate (secondary veins are clearly visible and branch off the midrib in a feather-like pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaflets reflect light, indicating a glossy surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis and petiole structures are relatively long, extending the leaflets away from the stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the rachis appears cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stems appear green, smooth, and flexible, typical of young seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the stems)
    19. Stem color: green (the stems are predominantly green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stems appear smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: Several leaflets show small holes and brown spots, indicating minor damage.
